title: wiretap: Add a generic process information table
description:
Second of the series adding capture-time process attribution (design on wireshark-dev: https://lists.wireshark.org/archives/wireshark-dev/202609/msg00002.html; see #17525 and #1184; first MR: !26470; pcapng spec proposal: https://github.com/IETF-OPSAWG-WG/draft-ietf-opsawg-pcap/pull/209).

This MR generalises the per-file table that !19734 added for Apple's Darwin process information blocks into a table of `WTAP_BLOCK_PROCESS_INFORMATION` blocks, and adds a portable, OS-neutral way to store that information in a file: the body of the Process Information Block proposed in the spec PR (a 32-bit process ID plus the options `pib_name`, `pib_path`, `pib_cmdline`, `pib_ppid`, `pib_uid`, `pib_user`, `pib_uuid` and `pib_starttime`), carried, until a block type is assigned, in a Wireshark Custom Block under the Foundation's PEN 32622 with block entry type 3, in the format of https://wiki.wireshark.org/Development/PcapngCustom. Nothing produces these blocks yet; dumpcap will, in a later MR, once the socket-to-process lookup in wsutil exists. The dissector side (`frame.process.*` fields resolved against the table) is the next MR.

**What changes**

- `wiretap/pcapng-wireshark-custom.c` (new): the handler for custom blocks with PEN 32622. A process information entry is read into a `WTAP_BLOCK_PROCESS_INFORMATION` block and added to the file's table rather than returned as a record; entries of an unknown type are kept as opaque custom block records so they are copied as is. The writer produces the same block, with the entry (type, length, process ID, options) little-endian whatever the byte order of the section, as the wiki page requires.
- `wtap_opttypes.[ch]`: `WTAP_BLOCK_PROCESS_INFORMATION`, `wtapng_process_info_mandatory_t` (the process ID plus the pcapng block type the information was read from, so that it is written back in the same form) and the `OPT_PIB_*` options.
- `wtap.[ch]`, `wtap_module.h`, `file_access.c`: the Darwin-only `dpibs` table, `wtap_file_get_dpib_lookup_info()` and `dpibs_growing` become `pibs`, `wtap_file_get_num_pibs()` / `wtap_file_get_pib()` and `pibs_growing`, mirroring the DSB API.
- `pcapng-darwin-custom.c`: the legacy DPIB (0x80000001) is read into the same block type (its options 2 and 4 map to `OPT_PIB_NAME` / `OPT_PIB_UUID`) and written back as a DPIB, byte for byte as before for Apple's files. The block is now added to the table by a block processor after it has been read, as DSBs are, which also fixes a reference leak (the reader took an extra reference that nothing released). Its options are written with `pcapng_write_options()`, so a comment or custom option on the block is written rather than left as zero bytes, and unknown option codes are ignored instead of raising an error that was then swallowed together with the rest of the options.
- `pcapng.c`: an enterprise handler's parser may replace the custom block with one to be processed internally (`wblock->internal`), the custom option processor and custom block writer of a handler may be NULL, and `pcapng_write_internal_blocks()` writes the table before packets, as for DSBs and NRBs.
- `epan/file_packet_provider.c`: `epan_get_process_id/name/uuid()` read the generic table; `packet-darwin.c` is unchanged.
- `pcapng_module.h`: `PEN_WIRESHARK` and `WIRESHARK_CB_ENTRY_PROCESS_INFORMATION`. The wiki page says the authoritative registry of entry types lives in the source; I will add entry type 3 to the page once this is merged.
- Release notes: capture file support and the API change.

**Why a custom block, rather than a local block type or waiting for the spec**: the core reader only takes standardised block and option codes, Apple's local-use 0x80000001 shows why that matters, and the spec process may take a while. The wiki page describes exactly this interim container, and since the entry body is the proposed standard block body, the same reader and writer will serve the standard block once a code is assigned, and existing files keep working.

**Not in this MR**: mergecap still drops the table (as it did DPIBs before), since Darwin's per-packet references are indices that would need remapping across input files; a follow-up will handle merging together with the proposed `epb_pib_index` option. Fileshark dissection of the entry can be added if wanted; the tests use the existing `pcapng.cb.*` fields.

**Tests**

`test/captures/_gen_process_info_blocks.py` generates `process_info_wireshark_cb.pcapng` (a little-endian and a big-endian section with three process information entries, one with every option, one with a comment among the custom block's own options, plus a custom block with an unknown entry type) and `process_info_darwin_dpib.pcapng` (two DPIBs and packets referring to them). `TestFileFormatsPcapngProcessInformation` checks that the blocks are not returned as records, that the Darwin blocks resolve through `frame.darwin.process_info.*`, and that both kinds survive a rewrite through editcap: the Wireshark blocks byte for byte, except that a comment on the block itself is written inside the entry.

Built and tested on Windows (MSVC, Ninja, tshark-only build); suite_fileformats, suite_mergecap and suite_io pass.

@@ -0,0 +1,210 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+#
+# Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer
+# By Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
+# Copyright 1998 Gerald Combs
+#
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+"""Generate the pcapng process information block test captures.
+
+process_info_wireshark_cb.pcapng has a little-endian and a big-endian
+section, each with one Ethernet interface, with process information carried
+in Wireshark custom blocks (PEN 32622, block entry type 3), whose entries are
+little-endian in both sections:
+
+    Section 1 (little-endian):
+        PIB 0: process 1234, with every option and a comment in the entry
+        PIB 1: process 4321, with no options
+        Frame 1: UDP packet from process 1234 (epb_processid_threadid)
+        Frame 2: a Wireshark custom block with an unknown entry type (99),
+                 which is kept as an opaque custom block record
+        Frame 3: UDP packet from process 4321
+    Section 2 (big-endian):
+        PIB 2: process 77, with a name and a user ID in the entry and a
+               comment among the options of the custom block itself
+        Frame 4: UDP packet from process 77
+
+process_info_darwin_dpib.pcapng has one little-endian section with legacy
+Darwin process information blocks (block type 0x80000001), as written by
+Apple's tcpdump, and packets that refer to them:
+
+        DPIB 0: process 501 "mDNSResponder", with a UUID
+        DPIB 1: process 1 "launchd"
+        Frame 1: UDP packet with darwin_dpib_id 0
+        Frame 2: UDP packet with darwin_dpib_id 1
+
+The hex dump of the custom data of each Wireshark custom block (everything
+after the PEN), as needed by the tests, is printed.
+"""
+import os
+import struct
+
+SHB_TYPE = 0x0A0D0D0A
+IDB_TYPE = 0x00000001
+EPB_TYPE = 0x00000006
+CB_COPY_TYPE = 0x00000BAD
+LEGACY_DPIB_TYPE = 0x80000001
+BYTE_ORDER_MAGIC = 0x1A2B3C4D
+LINKTYPE_ETHERNET = 1
+
+OPT_ENDOFOPT = 0
+OPT_COMMENT = 1
+OPT_EPB_PROCESSID_THREADID = 8
+OPT_EPB_DARWIN_DPIB_ID = 32769
+
+OPT_PIB_NAME = 2
+OPT_PIB_PATH = 3
+OPT_PIB_CMDLINE = 4
+OPT_PIB_PPID = 5
+OPT_PIB_UID = 6
+OPT_PIB_USER = 7
+OPT_PIB_UUID = 8
+OPT_PIB_STARTTIME = 9
+
+OPT_DPIB_NAME = 2
+OPT_DPIB_UUID = 4
+
+PEN_WIRESHARK = 32622
+WIRESHARK_CB_ENTRY_PROCESS_INFORMATION = 3
+
+UUID = bytes.fromhex("6b8b4567327b23c6643c986966334873")
+
+
+def pad4(data: bytes) -> bytes:
+    return data + b"\x00" * (-len(data) % 4)
+
+
+def ipv4_checksum(header: bytes) -> int:
+    total = 0
+    for i in range(0, len(header), 2):
+        total += (header[i] << 8) | header[i + 1]
+    while total >> 16:
+        total = (total & 0xFFFF) + (total >> 16)
+    return (~total) & 0xFFFF
+
+
+def udp_packet(seq: int) -> bytes:
+    """A minimal Ethernet/IPv4/UDP packet with a 4-byte payload."""
+    payload = struct.pack(">I", seq)
+    udp = struct.pack(">HHHH", 40000, 40001, 8 + len(payload), 0) + payload
+    ip = struct.pack(">BBHHHBBH4s4s", 0x45, 0, 20 + len(udp), seq, 0, 64, 17, 0,
+                     bytes([10, 0, 0, 1]), bytes([10, 0, 0, 2]))
+    ip = ip[:10] + struct.pack(">H", ipv4_checksum(ip)) + ip[12:]
+    eth = bytes.fromhex("000000000002") + bytes.fromhex("000000000001") + b"\x08\x00"
+    return eth + ip + udp
+
+
+def options(endian: str, opts) -> bytes:
+    """Encode a list of (code, value) options, or nothing if the list is empty."""
+    if not opts:
+        return b""
+    out = b""
+    for code, value in opts:
+        out += struct.pack(endian + "HH", code, len(value)) + pad4(value)
+    return out + struct.pack(endian + "HH", OPT_ENDOFOPT, 0)
+
+
+def block(endian: str, block_type: int, body: bytes) -> bytes:
+    body = pad4(body)
+    total_length = 12 + len(body)
+    return (struct.pack(endian + "II", block_type, total_length) + body +
+            struct.pack(endian + "I", total_length))
+
+
+def shb(endian: str) -> bytes:
+    # Byte-order magic, major/minor version, section length (unspecified).
+    return block(endian, SHB_TYPE, struct.pack(endian + "IHHq", BYTE_ORDER_MAGIC, 1, 0, -1))
+
+
+def idb(endian: str) -> bytes:
+    # LinkType, reserved, SnapLen; no options, so if_tsresol is 10^-6.
+    return block(endian, IDB_TYPE, struct.pack(endian + "HHI", LINKTYPE_ETHERNET, 0, 65535))
+
+
+def epb(endian: str, timestamp_us: int, packet: bytes, opts) -> bytes:
+    body = struct.pack(endian + "IIIII", 0, timestamp_us >> 32, timestamp_us & 0xFFFFFFFF,
+                       len(packet), len(packet))
+    body += pad4(packet)
+    body += options(endian, opts)
+    return block(endian, EPB_TYPE, body)
+
+
+def wireshark_cb_custom_data(entry_type: int, entry_data: bytes, cb_opts: bytes = b"") -> bytes:
+    """The custom data of a Wireshark custom block: the entry, which is
+    little-endian whatever the byte order of the section, and the options
+    of the block, which are given already encoded."""
+    return struct.pack("<II", entry_type, len(entry_data)) + pad4(entry_data) + cb_opts
+
+
+def wireshark_cb(endian: str, custom_data: bytes) -> bytes:
+    return block(endian, CB_COPY_TYPE, struct.pack(endian + "I", PEN_WIRESHARK) + custom_data)
+
+
+def pib_entry(pid: int, opts) -> bytes:
+    """The body of a Process Information Block, little-endian."""
+    return struct.pack("<I", pid) + options("<", opts)
+
+
+def legacy_dpib(endian: str, pid: int, opts) -> bytes:
+    return block(endian, LEGACY_DPIB_TYPE, struct.pack(endian + "I", pid) + options(endian, opts))
+
+
+def write(name: str, data: bytes) -> None:
+    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), name)
+    with open(path, "wb") as f:
+        f.write(data)
+    print(f"wrote {path} ({len(data)} bytes)")
+
+
+def gen_wireshark_cb() -> None:
+    base_ts = 1_757_500_000_000_000  # 2025-09-10T10:26:40Z in microseconds
+    custom_data = [
+        wireshark_cb_custom_data(WIRESHARK_CB_ENTRY_PROCESS_INFORMATION, pib_entry(1234, [
+            (OPT_PIB_NAME, b"curl"),
+            (OPT_PIB_PATH, b"/usr/bin/curl"),
+            (OPT_PIB_CMDLINE, b"curl\x00https://example.com/"),
+            (OPT_PIB_PPID, struct.pack("<I", 1)),
+            (OPT_PIB_UID, struct.pack("<I", 1000)),
+            (OPT_PIB_USER, b"alice"),
+            (OPT_PIB_UUID, UUID),
+            (OPT_PIB_STARTTIME, struct.pack("<Q", 1767225600000000000)),
+            (OPT_COMMENT, b"first process"),
+        ])),
+        wireshark_cb_custom_data(WIRESHARK_CB_ENTRY_PROCESS_INFORMATION, pib_entry(4321, [])),
+        wireshark_cb_custom_data(99, b"hello"),
+        wireshark_cb_custom_data(WIRESHARK_CB_ENTRY_PROCESS_INFORMATION, pib_entry(77, [
+            (OPT_PIB_NAME, b"sshd"),
+            (OPT_PIB_UID, struct.pack("<I", 0)),
+        ]), options(">", [(OPT_COMMENT, b"section two")])),
+    ]
+    out = shb("<") + idb("<")
+    out += wireshark_cb("<", custom_data[0])
+    out += wireshark_cb("<", custom_data[1])
+    out += epb("<", base_ts + 1, udp_packet(1), [(OPT_EPB_PROCESSID_THREADID, struct.pack("<II", 1234, 0))])
+    out += wireshark_cb("<", custom_data[2])
+    out += epb("<", base_ts + 2, udp_packet(2), [(OPT_EPB_PROCESSID_THREADID, struct.pack("<II", 4321, 0))])
+    out += shb(">") + idb(">")
+    out += wireshark_cb(">", custom_data[3])
+    out += epb(">", base_ts + 3, udp_packet(3), [(OPT_EPB_PROCESSID_THREADID, struct.pack(">II", 77, 0))])
+    write("process_info_wireshark_cb.pcapng", out)
+    for i, data in enumerate(custom_data):
+        print(f"custom data {i}: {data.hex()}")
+
+
+def gen_darwin_dpib() -> None:
+    base_ts = 1_757_500_000_000_000
+    out = shb("<") + idb("<")
+    out += legacy_dpib("<", 501, [(OPT_DPIB_NAME, b"mDNSResponder"), (OPT_DPIB_UUID, UUID)])
+    out += legacy_dpib("<", 1, [(OPT_DPIB_NAME, b"launchd")])
+    out += epb("<", base_ts + 1, udp_packet(1), [(OPT_EPB_DARWIN_DPIB_ID, struct.pack("<I", 0))])
+    out += epb("<", base_ts + 2, udp_packet(2), [(OPT_EPB_DARWIN_DPIB_ID, struct.pack("<I", 1))])
+    write("process_info_darwin_dpib.pcapng", out)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    gen_wireshark_cb()
+    gen_darwin_dpib()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

@@ -253,6 +253,107 @@ class TestFileFormatsPcapngDsb:
         assert dsb1_contents == dsb1_out
         assert dsb2_contents == dsb2_out
 
+class TestFileFormatsPcapngProcessInformation:
+    '''pcapng process information blocks.
+
+    Process information carried in Wireshark custom blocks (PEN 32622, block
+    entry type 3) and in legacy Darwin process information blocks (block type
+    0x80000001) is read into the process information table of the file, not
+    returned as records, and written back in the same form.  The captures are
+    generated by test/captures/_gen_process_info_blocks.py.
+    '''
+    WIRESHARK_CAPTURE = 'process_info_wireshark_cb.pcapng'
+    DARWIN_CAPTURE = 'process_info_darwin_dpib.pcapng'
+
+    # The custom data (everything after the PEN) of each Wireshark custom
+    # block in WIRESHARK_CAPTURE, in file order, as the generator prints it.
+    PIB_0 = ('0300000094000000d2040000020004006375726c03000d002f7573722f62696e2f6375726c000000'
+             '040019006375726c0068747470733a2f2f6578616d706c652e636f6d2f000000050004000100000006000400'
+             'e803000007000500616c696365000000080010006b8b4567327b23c6643c986966334873090008000000faed'
+             '5172861801000d0066697273742070726f6365737300000000000000')
+    PIB_1 = '0300000004000000e1100000'
+    UNKNOWN_ENTRY = '630000000500000068656c6c6f000000'
+    PIB_2 = '03000000180000004d00000002000400737368640600040000000000000000000001000b73656374696f6e2074776f0000000000'
+    # PIB 2 as written back: the comment among the options of the custom
+    # block itself moves into the (little-endian) entry, after its options.
+    PIB_2_REWRITTEN = '03000000280000004d0000000200040073736864060004000000000001000b0073656374696f6e2074776f0000000000'
+
+    def custom_blocks(self, cmd_tshark, path, env):
+        '''The (PEN, custom data) of the custom blocks in a pcapng file.'''
+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark,
+                '-r', path,
+                '-Xread_format:MIME Files Format',
+                '-Tfields',
+                '-e', 'pcapng.cb.pen',
+                '-e', 'pcapng.cb.custom_data',
+                '-Y', 'pcapng.cb.pen',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=env)
+        pens, data = stdout.strip().split('\t')
+        return list(zip(pens.split(','), data.split(',')))
+
+    def test_pcapng_pib_wireshark_cb_records(self, tshark_fields):
+        '''Process information blocks are not records; an unknown entry type is.'''
+        stdout = tshark_fields(self.WIRESHARK_CAPTURE, fields=('frame.number', 'frame.protocols'))
+        assert stdout.split('\n')[:4] == [
+            '1\teth:ethertype:ip:udp:data',
+            '2\tdata',
+            '3\teth:ethertype:ip:udp:data',
+            '4\teth:ethertype:ip:udp:data',
+        ]
+
+    def test_pcapng_pib_wireshark_cb_rewrite(self, cmd_tshark, cmd_editcap, capture_file, result_file, base_env):
+        '''Wireshark custom blocks are preserved while rewriting files.'''
+        infile = capture_file(self.WIRESHARK_CAPTURE)
+        outfile = result_file('process_info_wireshark_cb-rewritten.pcapng')
+        assert self.custom_blocks(cmd_tshark, infile, base_env) == [
+            ('32622', self.PIB_0),
+            ('32622', self.PIB_1),
+            ('32622', self.UNKNOWN_ENTRY),
+            ('32622', self.PIB_2),
+        ]
+        subprocess.run((cmd_editcap, infile, outfile), check=True, env=base_env)
+        assert self.custom_blocks(cmd_tshark, outfile, base_env) == [
+            ('32622', self.PIB_0),
+            ('32622', self.PIB_1),
+            ('32622', self.UNKNOWN_ENTRY),
+            ('32622', self.PIB_2_REWRITTEN),
+        ]
+
+    def test_pcapng_pib_darwin_fields(self, assert_frames_match):
+        '''Legacy Darwin process information blocks are looked up by the frame dissector.'''
+        assert_frames_match(self.DARWIN_CAPTURE, [
+            (1, 'frame.darwin.process_info.pid == 501 && frame.darwin.process_info.pname == "mDNSResponder"'),
+            (2, 'frame.darwin.process_info.pid == 1 && frame.darwin.process_info.pname == "launchd"'),
+        ])
+
+    def test_pcapng_pib_darwin_rewrite(self, cmd_tshark, cmd_editcap, capture_file, result_file, base_env):
+        '''Legacy Darwin process information blocks are written back as such.'''
+        infile = capture_file(self.DARWIN_CAPTURE)
+        outfile = result_file('process_info_darwin_dpib-rewritten.pcapng')
+        subprocess.run((cmd_editcap, infile, outfile), check=True, env=base_env)
+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark,
+                '-r', outfile,
+                '-Xread_format:MIME Files Format',
+                '-Tfields',
+                '-e', 'pcapng.block.type',
+                '-e', 'pcapng.darwin.process_id',
+                '-e', 'pcapng.darwin.process_name',
+                '-e', 'pcapng.darwin.process_uuid',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=base_env)
+        block_types, pids, names, uuids = stdout.strip().split('\t')
+        assert block_types.split(',').count('0x80000001') == 2
+        assert pids == '501,1'
+        assert names == 'mDNSResponder,launchd'
+        assert uuids == '6b8b4567-327b-23c6-643c-986966334873'
+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark,
+                '-r', outfile,
+                '-Tfields',
+                '-e', 'frame.darwin.process_info.pid',
+                '-e', 'frame.darwin.process_info.pname',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=base_env)
+        assert stdout.split('\n')[:2] == ['501\tmDNSResponder', '1\tlaunchd']
+
+
 class TestFileFormatMime:
     def test_mime_pcapng_gz(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
         '''Test that the full uncompressed contents is shown.'''

+/** @file
+ *
+ * Wiretap Library
+ * Copyright (c) 1998 by Gilbert Ramirez <gram@alumni.rice.edu>
+ *
+ * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+ */
+
+#ifndef __WTAP_PCAPNG_WIRESHARK_CUSTOM_H__
+#define __WTAP_PCAPNG_WIRESHARK_CUSTOM_H__
+
+#include "wtap.h"
+#include "wtap_opttypes.h"
+#include <stdbool.h>
+
+/**
+ * @brief Writes a process information block as a Wireshark custom block.
+ *
+ * @param wdh The wtap_dumper structure for the output file.
+ * @param pib The WTAP_BLOCK_PROCESS_INFORMATION block to write.
+ * @param err Pointer to an integer that will be set to an error code if an error occurs.
+ * @param err_info Pointer to a string where error information will be stored on failure.
+ * @return true if successful, false otherwise.

commits_data.title: wiretap: Add a generic process information table
commits_data.message:
wiretap: Add a generic process information table

Generalise the per-file table of Darwin process information blocks
into a table of WTAP_BLOCK_PROCESS_INFORMATION blocks, each holding a
process ID and options for the name, path, command line, parent
process ID, user ID, user name, executable UUID and start time of the
process, as proposed for a standard Process Information Block in the
pcapng specification:

    https://github.com/IETF-OPSAWG-WG/draft-ietf-opsawg-pcap/pull/209

Until a block type is assigned for it, carry that block body in a
Wireshark custom block (PEN 32622, block entry type 3), in the format
described at https://wiki.wireshark.org/Development/PcapngCustom, and
read Apple's Darwin process information block into the same table.
Each block is written back in the form in which it was read, so files
from Apple's tcpdump are rewritten as before, and custom blocks with
our PEN but an unknown entry type are kept as opaque records.

To do that, let the enterprise handler of a custom block replace the
block with one to be processed internally rather than returned as a
record, and let the custom option processor and custom block writer of
a handler be NULL. Add process information blocks to the table in a
block processor, once the block has been read, rather than in the
reader; that also fixes a leaked reference to each Darwin block. Write
the options of a Darwin block with pcapng_write_options(), so that
comments and custom options are written rather than left as zeroes,
and ignore unknown options in a Darwin block rather than treating them
as errors that are then discarded along with the rest of the options.

The epan_get_process_*() provider now looks the information up in the
generic table, so the Darwin frame dissector is unchanged.

Add generated captures with both kinds of block and tests for reading
them and for rewriting them through editcap.

Related to #1184 and #17525.
